QUOTE: The cancel pollers are the simplest case. Each one spins at 10 ms, reads an int or atomic, and sets an atomic `cancel_` flag. ... The C ABI passes only `int*`, so no `std::atomic` crosses the `.so` boundary.
VERDICT: MISS
WHY: The answer mentions cancel pollers and that the C ABI passes only `int*`, but never says the observer thread exists to bridge an atomic into a plain int because the ABI can't carry an atomic. It even describes the direction as reading an int and setting an atomic, which does not match the item.
